- **Best deck:** 8 zeros, then 6951423, 10985173, 12244371, 13020158, 13178745, 13241302, 13290499, 13297718. I found it by annealing, with n from 4 to 16 and card values up to 2^24.
- **Why decks stop near 0.388:** every card has weight 1/n, so mass at 0 can only change in steps of 1/16. The ladder law can set each weight freely, and that is where its advantage comes from.
- **Why the ladder law cannot grow:** with all-distinct partial sums, certification cost grows as about K⁴/6. On this machine, the 112-atom law took 21 s of CPU and 38–44 s of wall-clock time to certify. That is already over the 20 s limit, so more atoms are not possible.
- **Header:** the 5-line header in `strategy.py` records the best deck, its strict and tie fractions, the certified two-level value, and the open question of whether any law beats 0.400695. The editor shows type warnings in code inherited from the parent; the code runs correctly.
- **Confidence:** `confidence` gives 0.001 for (1, 1, 1, −2), and `report.json` contains `{"c1_1_1_-2": 0.001}`. The value is that low because 0.399323 is more than 1e-4 below the known 0.400695 limit, so it cannot be within 1e-4 of the supremum.

I stopped because I found no change that improves the certified value inside the time limit.
